title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
abstract: arXiv:2611.12356v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Speculative decoding speeds up language models by having a lightweight drafter propose future tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash predict an entire block in one forward pass, and DDTree builds draft trees directly from their per-position distributions. Each distribution implicitly assumes that the drafter's own greedy continuation is accepted, whereas a draft tree improves over a chain only on branches that leave this greedy path. Once a path forks, the drafter's top-1 accuracy drops from 89% to 18% and its top candidates often miss the true token. Re-running the drafter from the fork token largely restores its accuracy, showing that the errors stem from conditioning on an outdated prefix rather than from limited model capacity. translated_title: DForkTree：利用分叉感知的块扩散草稿树加速投机解码
translated_abstract: 投机解码通过让轻量级草稿模型提出未来token、再由目标模型并行验证的方式加速语言模型推理。块扩散草稿模型（如DFlash）可在一次前向传播中预测整个token块，而DDTree则直接基于其各位置的分布构建草稿树。每个分布都隐式地假设草稿模型自身的贪心延续会被接受，然而草稿树只有在偏离这条贪心路径的分支上才能优于链式结构。一旦路径发生分叉，草稿模型的top-1准确率会从89%骤降至18%，且其top候选往往无法命中真实token。实验表明，从分叉token处重新运行草稿模型可大幅恢复其准确率，这说明错误源于对过时前缀的条件化，而非模型能力有限。本文提出DForkTree，这是一种免训练方法，将每个分支重新锚定在其自身的token上，并通过逐点方式调整草稿模型的分数……
tldr: 提出免训练的DForkTree方法，通过分叉感知机制将草稿树的每个分支重新锚定在其自身token上，解决了块扩散草稿模型在路径分叉后条件化于过时前缀导致准确率大幅下降的问题，从而加速投机解码。
en_tdlr: DForkTree is a training-free method that accelerates speculative decoding by re-anchoring each draft tree branch on its own tokens with fork-awareness, addressing the accuracy collapse of block diffusion drafters caused by conditioning on outdated prefixes after forking.
